definition: Originally, a granary; now chiefly a farm or country estate, especially one associated with a large house.
etymology: It began with Latin granum, “grain.” From it came granica, a place for storing grain; Old French made this grange, and English adopted it in the Middle Ages—so the word’s stately modern sense grew out of a barn.
usage: By September, the grange was busy with carts bringing in the last of the grain.
